Header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-25 16:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Lena (CTO - Sunrise), Roberto (Head of Platform), Anika (Security), Mark (Product)

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: ok uh welcome everyone thanks for taking the time, this is Maya from Redwood inference, ill hand over to Evan for a short demo then we'll walk requirements, sound good?
00:18 Evan: cool thanks Maya, hi everyone, Evan SE on the runtime team, we'll demo JSON mode with a small tool invoke pattern — apologies if transcription butchered some names — we'll show how schemas and guardrails keep outputs typed so your ingestion pipeline doesn't break.
00:37 Lena: quick note, i'm mostly focused on reliability and data residency, low latency for our checkout personalization flows is top priority.
00:49 Roberto: also we'll need VPC option, we can't send raw PII out to hosted endpoints, that's a hard requirement.
01:02 Maya: totally understood, that's why we wanted to show both hosted and Dedicated/private options. ok Evan?
01:12 Evan: right jumping in — Console screen share now, show a request using JSON mode, schema definition on the left, generator on the right. Example: product_recommendation schema with typed array of items, each item has id, score, rationale. When tool calling happens we ask the model to return a typed action like {"call": "lookup_inventory", "args": {"sku": "..."}}.
01:37 Mark: so the model can proactively call back into our services? does that require additional hooks?
01:44 Evan: it's an orchestration pattern — you can set tool contracts in the Console; runtime will validate the JSON against schema and either allow execution or block, you also get a sandboxed dry-run in the Console. note: in some auto transcripts this gets logged as "tooling dry run" or "tried to do a lookup".
02:05 Anika: on security, does any of the PII leave our VPC in your private deployment?
02:12 Evan: in Private mode nothing leaves your VPC unless you configure a breakout, we have an option where control plane is separate, but KV cache and models run inside your environment, key mgmt via KMS/HSM integration — sorry sometimes docs call it K-M-S, but it's the standard KMS connectors.
02:33 Roberto: what about audit trails? we need per-request audit logs and token-level billing exported to our SIEM.
02:40 Priya: Console emits tracing and token-level breakdowns, you can stream logs to your logging endpoint and we support syslog/forwarding and S3 buckets for retention. There's also a per-request trace id to match to your trace.
02:56 Lena: latency numbers — what's typical for a 2-3 token turn, our SLA needs <120ms 95th for inference on dedicated hardware.
03:08 Evan: good question — on Dedicated with A100-class pools we see 15-80ms per token depending on sequence length. There is an important nuance: batch sizes and caching impact you. For personalization short sequences with prefix caching often land in the 40-100ms window. For guaranteed targets we recommend reserved Dedicated capacity or private racks.
03:34 Mark: And cost? obviously lower latency apples to higher cost right?
03:38 Maya: correct, tradeoff. Our Optimize recommendations suggest quantization + batching profiles to control unit costs. We'll include sample configs in the pilot spreadsheet.
03:50 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
03:57 Evan: demo continue — show schema fallback: if model returns malformed JSON runtime can auto-try a correction pass or route to a fallback model variant that is more permissive. This matters when your downstream is strict.
04:20 Roberto: does the fallback send anything outside the VPC?
04:23 Evan: no, fallback models can be pinned inside Dedicated/private clusters, the routing policy is customer controlled. Sometimes the automatic fallback is to a lower-cost hosted model if you opt-in, that's not recommended for PII.
04:38 Anika: SSO and identity, we use Okta and require SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning.
04:44 Maya: we support SAML and Okta provisioning; for Private we can enable SCIM and RBAC groups mapped to console roles.
04:52 Anika: SOC2? we need the report and pen test summary.
04:56 Priya: we can share SOC2 type II report, pen test summary, and our compliance pack — will attach in the follow up.
05:06 Mark: quick question on the tool execution model — if a model requests a call to 'lookup_inventory' how do you guarantee idempotency and prevent abuse?
05:16 Evan: we include function signatures and required args in the schema, runtime validates arg types and enforces rate limits and auth headers. There's also a policy engine to restrict calls in production.
05:29 Lena: timeline — we're looking for a pilot to start early march, 6 weeks to validate integration and perf, then a production rollout mid-April.
05:38 Maya: that's aligned with what we've seen. Pilot typically includes dedicated pool sizing, 1-2 integration endpoints, and agreed eval prompts + quality metrics.
05:48 Roberto: on networking, we need VPC peering and private link option, plus egress controls.
05:55 Evan: yep we'll provide our VPC peering guide, sample Terraform, and a runbook for peering — we'll walk through that in the infra deep dive with your platform team.
06:07 Anika: data retention policy — we'd like to disable retention of request/response in hosted mode and ensure logs are encrypted at rest.
06:15 Priya: in Private you control retention; hosted can be configured to not retain data and we have encryption at rest using KMS. We'll also share the retention config options.
06:26 Mark: show us the Console sandbox for schema editing?
06:29 Evan: sure. (screen) here's the schema editor; you can define a JSON schema, attach it to a model route, and set behavior on mismatch: FAIL, TRY_FIX, FALLBACK. See the JSON preview — sometimes the transcript shows curly braces as words in auto-captions.
06:49 Evan: i'm going to run a test prompt: "Given user context, propose three recommendations with shop-sku, score, and reason." Watch the output, it's typed.
07:02 Console (auto): 00:07 (test run) Model returned action: {"call":"lookup_inventory","args":{"sku":"SKU-123"}}
07:10 Evan: runtime validated schema, then invoked the mock tool in the sandbox — the Console returns execution logs and the typed result back in the same trace.
07:22 Roberto: if we want to wire our real inventory system, what's the auth workflow?
07:26 Evan: you can provide short-lived tokens via vault or sign requests with a customer-managed HMAC; for Private we allow direct service account mapping.
07:36 Anika: any concerns about secrets being mishandled in long-lived caches?
07:40 Evan: KV cache is configurable; we recommend encrypting cache entries and rotating keys. For sensitive attributes we set a zero-ttl cache policy. Sometimes the spoken note will say "KV cash" but docs use KV cache.
07:57 Lena: I want to see a failover story — if Dedicated pool is under pressure what happens?
08:05 Maya: you can set a routing policy that falls back to a compatible model (e.g., smaller quantized variant) or route to Hosted as last resort, and you can set hard blocks for PII to prevent egress.
08:20 Roberto: okay, cost controls—can we set per-route quotas and alerts?
08:25 Priya: yes, token-level quotas, budget alerts, and automatic throttles. We'll show the Console billing view in follow-up.
08:33 Mark: about schema evolution: our product has frequent changes, do we need to redeploy models when schema changes?
08:39 Evan: no you can version schemas independently; the runtime can validate against multiple versions and route by header or route config. We suggest a canary approach with A/Bing in the Console.
08:54 Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
09:01 Evan: now quick show of Optimize recommendations — runtime will look at your traffic profile and suggest batch sizes, kv caching lifetimes, and quantization profiles that meet latency/cost targets. It's a report we can generate from sample traffic.
09:20 Mark: will you run a sample optimization run on our logs?
09:24 Maya: yes we can do a non-prod ingest to produce an Optimize report in week 1 of the pilot. We'll need a representative traffic dump.
09:34 Anika: what about regulatory region locking, we have EU customers and need data to live in eu-west only.
09:41 Evan: Private deployments support region-locking; hosted has regional endpoints and you can pin processing to eu-west, we will include data residency options in the pilot scope.
09:52 Rob: are there established SLAs for Dedicated?
09:56 Maya: yes Dedicated comes with SLA tiers tied to commit level; we will include latency SLOs as part of the contract for pilot if you choose reserved capacity.
10:07 Lena: I heard you mention model variants for fallback — are those open weights or Redwood-managed base models?
10:13 Evan: we support both. You can bring open models or use Redwood-curated model variants tuned for runtime. For private we can help you onboard your own models.
10:24 Mark: anything special for debugging when schema mismatches occur?
10:28 Evan: Console exposes raw traces, the model output, parser errors and optionally a suggested patch. We also capture token-level cost so you can see where regressions come from.
10:40 Maya: quick pause for questions?
10:42 Roberto: if our infra team needs a test account for peering, who do they reach out to?
10:47 Evan: send me an email and we'll create a staging Private account and an infra playbook. I'll include sample Terraform and a demo peering runbook.
10:58 Anika: about encryption keys — do you integrate with Azure Key Vault?
11:03 Priya: we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSM via standard interfaces. We'll share the integration doc.
11:12 Lena: okay next — run a failure scenario where model returns malformed JSON and we show the fix?
11:18 Evan: will do. Running the malformed response test: model outputs missing comma, runtime parses error, auto-correction attempt, then fallback to strict model which returns corrected JSON.
11:36 Console: (auto note) Attempt 1: parse error / Attempt 2: try_fix succeeded / Final: validated response
11:44 Mark: nice — that try_fix behavior is useful but what are the guarantees?
11:48 Evan: try_fix is best-effort, not guaranteed. For strict pipelines set mismatch action to FAIL and rely on canary routing and human-in-the-loop.
11:58 Speaker 3: (murmur)
12:05 Maya: next steps recap — we'll send pilot scope, SOC2 pack, sample Terraform, and schedule infra deep dive.
12:14 Lena: for timelines, if we get docs by Friday we can start in first week of march.
12:20 Maya: perfect. Anything else from Sunrise?
12:24 Roberto: one last onbench — can you include a rough sizing/guesstimate for dedicated pool cost for 5k RPS?
12:33 Priya: we'll run a cost model and include in the pricing spreadsheet; note that 5k RPS will probably need autoscaling and multiple pods — we'll give a range.
12:45 Mark: thanks folks, i liked the schema editor, looks like it'll reduce our ETL brittle points.
12:50 Anika: thanks — please include pen test summary.
12:53 Maya: will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack.
13:00 Meeting end (call wraps).
